subsystems.name: Individual robot unit
subsystems.role: the repeated, deliberately simple element — cheap enough that losing some is acceptable.
parts: chassis, motors and wheels or rotors

subsystems.name: Localisation and sensing
subsystems.role: lets each unit know roughly where it is and where its neighbours are, usually without satellite positioning.
parts: GNSS where the sky is visible

subsystems.name: Communication mesh
subsystems.role: neighbour-to-neighbour radio links that relay messages across the group with no central tower.

subsystems.name: Coordination software
subsystems.role: identical rules running on every unit, using only local information, that add up to a useful collective behaviour.

subsystems.name: Operator interface
subsystems.role: one person tasks and supervises a whole swarm rather than piloting each unit.

subsystems.name: Support infrastructure
subsystems.role: keeps dozens to hundreds of units charged, transported and repaired.

buildSteps.title: Define the collective task
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the swarm must achieve — map an area, find a target, move material — and work out the minimum each robot must sense and do to contribute.

buildSteps.title: Design the unit for cost and repair
buildSteps.detail: Simplicity is the point: a unit that costs a few hundred dollars can be fielded in hundreds and replaced rather than mended. Use commodity motors, chips and sensors.

buildSteps.title: Choose how units locate themselves
buildSteps.detail: Outdoors, GNSS plus inertial dead reckoning. Indoors or underground, ultra-wideband ranging between units or visual markers, accepting that accuracy degrades in cluttered spaces.

buildSteps.title: Build the radio mesh
buildSteps.detail: Fit each unit with a low-power radio, a routing protocol that survives units dropping out, and tight time synchronisation so messages can be slotted without collisions.

buildSteps.title: Write decentralised control rules
buildSteps.detail: Every unit runs the same short rule set — stay apart, drift toward neighbours, follow the local gradient of a task — so no central computer is needed and the swarm keeps working when some units fail.

buildSteps.title: Simulate thousands of agents
buildSteps.detail: Run the rules in a simulator with radio and sensor noise before cutting metal, because emergent behaviour is hard to predict and bugs appear only at scale.

buildSteps.title: Trial at tens, then hundreds
buildSteps.detail: Field tests expose what simulation hides: radio congestion, battery spread, units colliding, and the difficulty of getting them all deployed and recovered.

buildSteps.title: Add human supervision
buildSteps.detail: Give one operator a tasking view, a live picture of the swarm, and a reliable stop command that reaches every unit.

buildSteps.title: Scale manufacturing and upkeep
buildSteps.detail: Set up batch production, charging routines and firmware updates, since maintenance of hundreds of units is the real cost of ownership.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap microcontrollers, MEMS sensors and brushless motors
prerequisites.why: swarm behaviour only makes sense when a single unit is inexpensive enough to mass-produce.

prerequisites.tech: Low-power mesh radio with time synchronisation
prerequisites.why: neighbour-to-neighbour communication without a base station is what makes coordination decentralised.
ultra-wideband and vision work in open or mapped spaces but degrade indoors, underground and in rubble.

prerequisites.tech: Onboard perception within a tight power budget
prerequisites.why: small units must recognise terrain, people or ore with milliwatts, not server racks.
a swarm that must be collected by hand every hour cannot work at scale.

prerequisites.tech: Rules for operating many autonomous vehicles at once
prerequisites.why: aviation, road and mining regulators have no settled framework for hundreds of independent machines in one place.

pathway.milestone: laboratory swarms of a thousand simple robots demonstrating self-assembly and collective transport
pathway.unlocks: confidence that decentralised rules scale without a central controller.

pathway.milestone: field pilots in search and rescue, agriculture and inspection with tens to a few hundred units
pathway.unlocks: real operating experience with radio congestion, terrain and recovery.

pathway.milestone: mixed swarms of a few capable robots and many simple ones sharing one map
pathway.unlocks: tasks too varied for identical units, such as surveying then excavating.

pathway.milestone: planetary mining swarms operating without continuous contact with Earth
pathway.unlocks: resource extraction where a single large machine would be too risky to lose and too heavy to land.
